item.title: Deploying and Using OpenClaw
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
https://docs.openclaw.ai/

Deploying OpenClaw

Server and system setup

Tencent Cloud Lighthouse instance: 4 CPU cores, 4GB RAM, 70GB system disk

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 64-bit — ChatGPT recommended this as the most compatible option.

Installing OpenClaw

Update the system and install dependencies

# Update the system
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
# Install base dependencies
sudo apt install -y git curl wget unzip build-essential
# Install nvm
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
source ~/.bashrc
# Install Node.js
nvm install --lts
nvm use --lts
# Verify the install and check versions
node -v
npm -v

Install OpenClaw

npm install -g openclaw@latest

Start OpenClaw

# Initialise config and install
openclaw onboard --install-daemon
# install-daemon registers the OpenClaw Gateway as a background daemon: it runs
# silently, starts on boot, and restarts itself if it crashes

item.description:
AI Agents, From Chatbot to Production

An AI agent is the LLM application taken further — something that can plan on its own, carry out tasks, and interact with its environment.

Foundational papers:

  • Yao, S., et al. (2022). “ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models.” ICLR. [paper] — the ReAct framework, the core pattern behind most agents
  • Wei, J., et al. (2022). “Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models.” NeurIPS. [paper]
  • Wang, G., et al. (2024). “A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents.” arXiv. [paper] — a survey of the agent landscape
